title: How heatwaves impact people with disabilities
description:
Heatwaves are uncomfortable for everyone. But people living with disabilities face additional and specific challenges that can compromise their health and well-being. Many of these issues - from struggling service dogs to overheating wheelchairs - are frequently overlooked, even in public advice and emergency planning.

Maddie Molloy is a BBC climate and science reporter who is also profoundly deaf. She explains some of the challenges a heatwave can pose for deaf people, the visually impaired and people who use wheelchairs. We also hear from Blessing Odukoya, Emily Davison, Maddie Haining and Osayuki Igbinoba about how they cope with the heat.

summaryZh: 本集談到熱浪（heatwave）對身心障礙者與有健康狀況者的特殊影響。主持人訪問了資深氣候記者兼重度聽障者Maddie，她說她和她的助聽犬Cole在高溫下都很難適應。節目說明：輪椅使用者會遇到椅布悶熱、金屬把手與輪子燙手、電池快速沒電；截肢者的義肢襯墊（liner）會悶熱造成紅疹與熱疹；視障者在強光下可能失去餘光；人工電子設備（如人工耳蝸、電池）在高溫中可能故障。受訪者提到公共交通缺乏空調、電梯故障會讓人被困、以及導致更多疲勞。建議包括在政策與緊急規劃中納入更多不同障礙者的聲音，改善無障礙交通、提供充電與備援方案、並提醒保持補水與降溫等個人應對策略。
summaryEn: This episode explains how heatwaves make life harder for people with disabilities. Guests include Maddie, a BBC climate reporter who is profoundly deaf, and other disabled people. Problems described: wheelchairs get hot (fabric, metal, wheels), batteries and medical devices can fail, prosthetic liners trap heat, guide or hearing dogs also suffer, and public transport or lifts failing can leave people stuck. Solutions suggested: include disabled people's voices in planning, improve accessibility (air conditioning, charging, backup plans), and give practical tips like staying cool and hydrated.

vocabulary.meaningZh: 熱浪，長時間的高溫天氣
vocabulary.definitionEn: A period of unusually hot weather lasting several days or more.
A chair on wheels used by someone who cannot walk or has difficulty walking.
vocabulary.example: push myself in my manual wheelchair

vocabulary.definitionEn: Relating to an artificial body part (or the artificial part itself).
A thin layer or covering placed inside something (here, inside a prosthetic) for comfort or protection.
vocabulary.example: I wear liners which are made of silicone

vocabulary.definitionEn: Extreme tiredness or exhaustion, often physical or mental.

vocabulary.meaningZh: （在此為）快速耗盡、消失（字面意為蒸發）
vocabulary.definitionEn: Disappearing or being used up quickly (literally turning from liquid into vapor).
vocabulary.example: their batteries just like completely evaporating

vocabulary.definitionEn: The quality of being easy to reach, use, or enter, especially for people with disabilities.

vocabulary.meaningZh: 被隔離、被關在某處（通常短期、不方便活動）
vocabulary.definitionEn: Kept away or isolated, often in a place where movement is limited.
vocabulary.example: we've been sort of sequestered at home

vocabulary.meaningZh: 耳蝸的（常見於“cochlear implant”人工耳蝸）
vocabulary.definitionEn: Relating to the cochlea in the inner ear; used in terms like cochlear implant (a device helping hearing).
Open or painful spots on the skin caused by irritation, pressure, or infection.
vocabulary.example: can actually start to cause sores on your skin

phrases.meaningZh: 助聽犬（提醒失聰者注意聲音）
phrases.definitionEn: A trained assistance dog that alerts a deaf or hard-of-hearing person to important sounds.
phrases.example: I have a hearing dog as well

phrases.definitionEn: Dogs trained to help visually impaired people move around safely.

phrases.meaningZh: 長時間被困在室內造成的煩悶或焦躁
phrases.definitionEn: Irritation or restlessness from being confined indoors for a long time.
phrases.example: feeling a bit of cabin fever

phrases.definitionEn: Relax and avoid doing too much; rest when needed.
To be left in a place without a way to leave, often unexpectedly.
An alternative plan to be used if the first plan fails.
